AudioUploadRequest.description:
Ask permission to upload one chunk of an encounter's audio.

The `chunk_id` is client-stamped (D5.3 doctrine, same as `event_id` and
`patient_id`), so re-sending this request is a *re-send*, not a second chunk:
the server answers out of the ledger row the first attempt created.
`chunk_index` + `is_final` are the §C3 ordering contract, and `content_type`
gets signed into the returned URL — whatever you declare here is exactly what
your `PUT` must send, byte for byte, or S3 rejects the signature (§C1).

PHI-minimal by construction (§C5): there is no field for a filename, a label,
or any human text — four scalars, two of them opaque ids.

chunk_index.description:
0-based and contiguous per encounter. `u32`, not the row's `i32`: this is
the one audio field a client *sends*, so serde refusing `-1` at the door is
validation the handler then never has to write.

content_type.description:
From S3's allowlist: `audio/wav` | `audio/ogg` | `audio/mp4` | `audio/mpeg`.
Declared per chunk; nothing in the pipeline hardcodes a container (D6.15).

is_final.description:
Exactly one chunk per encounter carries `true` — the one cut when the
clinician tapped stop, so its index is the highest. Finality is data on a
chunk rather than a separate RPC, which is what lets it survive retries and
out-of-order arrival like everything else (§C3).

AudioUploadRequest.title: AudioUploadRequest

AudioUploadResponse.description:
The valet key (§C1).

Nothing here reveals anything about the patient, but `upload_url` *is* a bearer
credential for one `PUT` to one key: log the `chunk_id`, never the URL.

chunk_id.description:
Echoed back so a client that pipelines several intents can match answers to
requests without relying on ordering.

expires_in_secs.description:
900 (15 minutes). A client that has sat on a URL should re-ask rather than
hoard it: re-issuing an intent is idempotent and costs one round trip.

upload_url.description:
Presigned `PUT` straight to object storage — the API never handles a byte of
audio, and the URL carries its own authorization.

AudioUploadResponse.title: AudioUploadResponse

AuditEntry.description: Immutable audit log entry — append-only, never modified.

CaptureMode.description: How the audio was captured — affects summarization strategy.

oneOf.description: In the room with the patient — may include patient speech, ambient noise.
Clinician dictating privately (hallway, workstation) — single-speaker, structured.

ChunkView.description:
One chunk's ledger state. The completion ack and the status read (both S4,
driven by S8's poll loop) return this same shape, so a client has one thing to
learn and one thing to render.

Deliberately *not* a mirror of the `audio_chunks` row: `org_id`, `s3_key`, and
the per-chunk `transcript` stay server-side. The device already knows its org,
has no use for the key, and does not read transcripts here at all — it reads
them the way it reads everything else, as a worker-authored `TranscriptReady`
event off the S5 cursor, once the *whole* encounter has been assembled (§C4).

duration_ms.description:
Audio length in milliseconds, from the STT provider's metadata; `None` until
a worker finishes the chunk. Step 7's `usage_log` meters from this (D6.13).

Stays `i32` — the row's own type — while `chunk_index` widens to `u32`,
because the two have different provenance. `chunk_index` came *from* a `u32`
this server accepted, so converting it back is provably safe; `duration_ms`
is written by the worker under no such guarantee, and keeping it in the
storage type means the boundary needs no fallible cast for a value nobody
does arithmetic on.

error.description:
Terminal failure reason, `None` while healthy. Operator-facing text for the
§C2 autopsy — never transcript content.

status.description:
One of [`chunk_status`]. Unrecognized values are possible against a newer
server and should be treated as "still moving", not as an error.

ChunkView.title: ChunkView

ClinicalResult.description:
A clinical result — lab, imaging, or vital sign.
Field shapes mirror FHIR R4 Observation so future integration is a mapping layer.

Disposition.description: ED disposition — the most important single field in an ED note.

Encounter.description: A single encounter snippet — one recording session for one patient.

encounter_number.description: Encounter number for this patient (1st visit, 2nd visit, etc.)

EventAck.description:
Per-event acknowledgment: the server-assigned position in the stream.
On a duplicate delivery this is the ORIGINAL sequence_id — same answer every time.

EventDown.description: One event coming down — the wire twin of er_store's StoredEvent envelope.

EventsPage.description: A page of the stream. `has_more` tells the client to keep looping (§C3).
EventsPage.title: EventsPage

JobView.description:
PHI-free status projection for asynchronous work. Generated clinical content
is delivered only through the event stream.
JobView.title: JobView

LabResult.description: A lab result with FHIR-ready fields.

fhir_id.description: FHIR resource ID, if pulled from EMR. None = manually entered.

loinc_code.description: LOINC code for the lab test (e.g., "2160-0" for creatinine).

MdmRequest.description:
Request server-owned MDM generation. The client stamps the id so a timed-out
POST can be retried without creating or billing a second job.
MdmRequest.title: MdmRequest

NoteEvent.description: Events that drive the note state machine and the processing pipeline.

oneOf.description: Clinician started recording for a patient.

AI produced/updated note prose from an
encounter transcript.
A clinical result was ingested (manual or FHIR).
AI produced the MDM from accumulated data.
MDM draft is ready for review.

NotePhase.description:
Patient note lifecycle — supports cycles (Idle ↔ Encountering).

Valid transition graph:
```text
  Registered ──AudioStart──▶ Encountering
                                   │
                               AudioStop
                                   │
                                   ▼
                                 Idle ◀──────────────┐
                                ╱    ╲               │
                      AudioStart    TriggerMDM   AudioStop
                              ╱          ╲           │
                             ▼            ▼          │
                      Encountering    Finalizing ──▶ │
                                         │
                                      ReviewReady
                                         │
                                         ▼
                                   PendingSignOff
                                         │
                                       Sign
                                         ▼
                                       Signed
```

oneOf.description: Clinician in room or dictating — audio live.
Between encounters — waiting on data or seeing other patients.
Clinician triggered MDM/dispo — assembling final note.

NoteSectionVersion.description: A versioned note section snapshot — retained for audit trail.

NoteSections.description: The sections that compose an ED note.

NoteView.description:
The read model for clients. A deliberate DTO (§C1): PatientNote can gain/rename
fields freely; only NoteView::from must keep up, and the compiler enforces that.
NoteView.title: NoteView

PatientNote.description:
The complete patient note — the central domain object.

Holds both a `NotePhase` enum (for serialization) and a `Box<dyn NoteState>`
trait object (for behavior). They are kept in sync by the `handle_*` methods.

RegisterPatientRequest.description:
PHI-minimal BY CONSTRUCTION (§C1): no name, no age, no MRN — no fields to put them in.
`display_label` is "Room 4 – chest pain" territory, never an identity.
RegisterPatientRequest.title: RegisterPatientRequest

ResultSource.description: How a result entered the system.

info.description: Synthetic staging contract. 60 requests/minute per clinician, plus 5 MDM and 30 audio intents/minute. Stable event/job/chunk IDs are required on retries. See docs/api-contract.md.
info.title: ER Note API
